engine_bytes.rule: The board pins the engine inputs by sha256 (evaluation_engine_inputs and the files named by the engine command). The placeholders resolve to an export of spellbench bb20077 for the adapter files, the pinned python.exe, the pinned catalog and the pinned bridge. Before `bench commit`, run `spellbench bench prepare benchmarks/pauper-ladder-v3 --check` from a clean checkout of the default branch, with the pinned python.exe and with every placeholder resolved from benchmarks/local.json: it must print OK. The check prepares the definition again and compares the bytes, so both engine identities (the base form's and the export blocks'), the nine bot identities and the schedule are the committed ones; it refuses any placeholder of the definition that is also set in the process environment (usually MTG_KERNEL_V2_BRIDGE and MTG_KERNEL_PUBLIC_CATALOG; remove MTG_KERNEL_V2_SOURCE too), and the builtin bot identities hash the interpreter and the checkout's builtin bot sources. Drive `bench commit` and `bench run` the same way. A commitment cannot be redone.
engine_bytes.prepare_check: `bench prepare --check` on this definition, 2026-11-15, in a scratch copy with the pinned python.exe and the bridge, catalog and source variables removed from the process: OK (the committed bytes are the prepared bytes). With the bridge and catalog variables set it refused; under another interpreter it reported the two builtin bot identities as different. board.validity: Enforced by code (unit spellbench-validity/v1 in benchmark.json, docs/design/2026-11-15-validity-unit.md). Every denominator is the scheduled count. Per block: at least 125 of 128 games natural and at least 63 of 64 pairs complete. Per bot: at least 97% of its scheduled games natural. Per ordered deck pairing over the run: at least 33 of 36 games natural (90%, one game always allowed). Forfeits of any cause, halts, truncations and games not played count against natural. `bench run` writes the verdict and the tables into the manifest. A failing run is published in full and revealed, is not rated, shows no rating, is excluded by its own record, and is never topped up or replaced: bench prepare does not schedule its matchups again under this evaluation. `bench compose` applies the unit again to the blocks it combines.
board.number: A rating is Elo against the reference bots over every ordered pairing of the eight decks. Unequal decks pull scores toward even, so the scale is this board's own: no v3 number is compared with a pauper-ladder-v2 or pauper-grid-v1 number. Per-deck ratings are not published (deck_slices false).

infoset_off.ruling: Evaluation 3.0.0 runs without x_kernel_infoset_v1. The exporter halts with engine_fault:infoset:I1 when a token is returned to its owner's hand and a decision is posed before it ceases to exist (Snap on an opposing token; mtg-kernel#713). None of the 252 mirror games of the sweep reached it. No scheduled bot reads the export. A bot that needs it (the search entrant) joins later through a per-block opt-in under a new evaluation version, with the exporter fixed first. Evaluation 3.0.0 does not offer per-block extensions and does not forbid them: the extensions are a field of the definition and of the snapshot contract, and a later evaluation version defines the opt-in.

play_is_unchanged.what: The same scheduled games (same config, run secret, game secrets and bot seeds) played with the extension and without it, the engine traffic recorded by a line tap. Sample 1: the sweep run above with the extension, its 18 halted games and 25 natural Faeries off-mirror games. Sample 2: this board's 18 blocks under a fresh secret, 3 off-mirror pairs in each block: 108 games, 54 ordered deck pairings, every deck on the play and on the draw, every scheduled bot.
play_is_unchanged.natural_games_result: every ledger field equal except game_digest, which chains the engine traffic and so names the enabled extensions; the traffic is identical message for message once the extension's own payload and name are removed, with the one field the information-set path adds to the x_kernel_flat_v4 payload (known_hand_masked_observation_sha256, read only by the search bot) and the request ids (counters, which the game digest leaves out too)
play_is_unchanged.halted_games_result: each matches the game without the extension message for message up to the request the halt answered, and ends naturally without it

v4_visibility.what_it_tests: At every decision of neutral private-support games on the eight board decks, the acting seat's V4 boundary and x_kernel_flat_v4 encoding are unchanged when the search sampler redeterminizes every hidden card the engine's knowledge tables mark as unknown to that seat; and every place one player learned hidden cards of the other (library look or reveal, hand reveal, library reorder revealed to the opponent) is a reviewed site marked in the source. It is a consistency check against the engine's own knowledge tables plus a pinned enumeration of reveal sites, not a proof against a fact the tables wrongly mark as known.

export_blocks.validity: The same unit (spellbench-validity/v1), by code. The entrant-only run: each block at least 125 of 128 natural and 63 of 64 complete pairs; the entrant 373 of 384, each opponent 125 of 128; each ordered deck pairing 5 of 6. A halted or truncated game breaks its pair, so two such games in different pairs fail a block. The composed snapshot is judged as a whole (21 blocks; each ordered deck pairing 38 of 42). A failing run is revealed and recorded as excluded; its blocks are not played again under this version, and a base block that failed stays barred.
export_blocks.snapshot: A snapshot that holds blocks of both forms has schema spellbench-snapshot/v2: its top level is the base form's contract and engine facts, and one object, export_blocks, carries the export form's contract, engine facts and matchups. A snapshot without an export-form block is written as before, to the byte. A new snapshot refits every rating over all 21 blocks.

rule: Rerun every audit above on the pinned binaries, and replace this receipt, whenever the engine behind this board changes. The board rates no games on an engine without a passing receipt.
